minutes.headline: Council on Aging heard the plan for a new town hall and Ritter building renovation; only minutes and adjournment were voted.
minutes.summary: The board approved prior minutes, reviewed the level-funded FY26 COA budget and its thin program funds, and heard updates on the medical center provider, kitchen renovation and events. A presenter from the Municipal Building Design Committee walked through a town hall, Ritter building and meeting house plan and took questions on cost and tax impact. The meeting then adjourned.

budget_items.what_was_said: Level funded apart from salaries, with an added amount to cover a software/service cost moved under the COA budget.
Two part-time kitchen aides are paid from the formula grant rather than the town budget, and the director will ask the Finance Committee to move them into the town budget.
The whole program budget for the year is very small.
The entire budget to run the center was stated.
Program budget is nearly exhausted for the rest of the fiscal year, and donations were requested.
Presenter gave earlier and current cost estimates, likely a 20-year bond, with tax impact still being calculated.
A federal incentive could cover part of solar panel cost but is on hold.
Presenter said costs rise about every two years if the project is delayed.

decisions.decision: Whether to change how minutes are distributed (mail vs email) will be put on the next agenda.
The director will make a plea to the Finance Committee on February 20th to move the kitchen aides into the town budget.
The two part-time meal site positions will be combined into one 36-hour position, allowing Meals on Wheels on Fridays.
The board was advised to engage with DPW on the parking lot architectural plan scope.

what_happened.line: The Council on Aging heard a Municipal Building Design Committee presentation on a town hall, Ritter building and meeting house plan, with questions on cost and tax impact.
The presenter said the project would likely be financed by a 20-year bond, with the tax impact still being calculated.
The board reviewed a level-funded FY26 COA budget apart from salaries, and heard that the program budget is nearly exhausted for the rest of the fiscal year.
The director plans to ask the Finance Committee on February 20th to move two kitchen aides, now paid from the formula grant, into the town budget.
No votes were recorded on the building plan; the only items voted were prior minutes and adjournment.

why_it_matters: A town hall and Ritter building project financed by a bond would reach residents' tax bills, and the presenter said the amount is still being worked out, so a vote on it is likely to come later.

Whether the kitchen aides are paid from the town budget or the formula grant affects how the senior center's meal and program staffing is funded, and the Finance Committee request is where that is decided.
watch_next: February 20th: the director's request to the Finance Committee to move the kitchen aides into the town budget.
Next Council on Aging agenda: whether minutes are distributed by mail or email.
